nodes.name: Gaucher disease
nodes.description: Gaucher disease (GD) is a lysosomal storage disorder encompassing three main forms (types 1, 2 and 3), a fetal form and a variant with cardiac involvement (Gaucher disease - ophthalmoplegia - cardiovascular calcification or Gaucher-like disease).

nodes.name: Fabry disease
nodes.description: Fabry disease (FD) is a progressive, inherited, multisystemic lysosomal storage disease characterized by specific neurological, cutaneous, renal, cardiovascular, cochleo-vestibular and cerebrovascular manifestations.

nodes.name: Niemann-Pick disease type A
nodes.description: Niemann-Pick disease type A is a very severe subtype of Niemann-Pick disease, an autosomal recessive lysosomal disease, and is characterized clinically by onset in infancy or early childhood with failure to thrive, hepatosplenomegaly, and rapidly progressive neurodegenerative disorders.

nodes.description: A rare lysosomal storage disorder characterized by intralysosomal accumulation of sulfatides in various tissues, leading to progressive deterioration of motor and neurocognitive function.

nodes.name: mucolipidosis type II
nodes.description: Mucolipidosis II (MLII) is a slowly progressive lysosomal disorder characterized by growth retardation, skeletal abnormalities, facial dysmorphism, stiff skin, developmental delay and cardiomegaly.

nodes.name: glycogen storage disease II

nodes.name: Sandhoff disease
nodes.description: A lysosomal disorder from the GM2 gangliosidosis family, caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in the HEXB gene, characterized by GM2 ganglioside accumulation in the nervous system and progressive central nervous system degeneration.

Niemann-Pick disease type A and Niemann-Pick disease, type C1 are both lysosomal disorders sharing 3 annotated phenotypes.
edges.state: Both Niemann-Pick disease type A (genes: SMPD1) and Niemann-Pick disease, type C1 (genes: NPC1) are lysosomal disorders. Shared HPO phenotypes: Sea-blue histiocytosis, Hypotonia, Bone-marrow foam cells. Both disrupt lysosomal function, though via different genes; phenotype overlap may reflect shared downstream lysosomal pathology or may be generic (e.g. hepatosplenomegaly is common across storage disorders).
